shared_turn_1.user_message: Why is there a risk of rejection of donated organs, but not of donated blood?
shared_turn_1.assistant_response:
Organ rejection happens because transplanted organs contain living cells with foreign surface proteins (HLA/MHC antigens). Your immune system recognizes these as “non-self” and attacks the tissue.

Donated blood is different: red blood cells have no nuclei and don’t present antigens the way organ cells do. If blood types are compatible, they aren’t recognized as foreign tissue. They also circulate briefly and are cleared naturally. Blood can still cause reactions if types are mismatched, but it doesn’t trigger the same ongoing immune rejection as an organ transplant.
